question: Would a site about <niche> plausibly publish a page about this topic for its readers? Borderline counts as no.
method: Re-run for the Worker tools. The lists are the top 20 rows returned by POST /v1/profile/trends (trends_for_profile) for the three sample profiles in the United States, India and Brazil, served by the built shards of the real 2026-11-01 data (the same Worker code as production, run with `wrangler dev --local`). The matcher is match.js, so the lists equal the page's lists (checked: 8 of 9 lists identical to the browser's top 50 at fit 0.35 and above; the ninth lacks 4 title-only rows at 0.40, see docs/personalization.md). Each niche's distinct rows were given alphabetically, with only the topic name and its Wikidata description and the niche, to one model call (`completion`, default model, no tools or history) that answered true or false per row. The typed judge (`judge_batch`) was tried first and was unavailable (its provider rejected the account), so it is a model call, not an independent human or subagent. Same rule as before: borderline counts as no.
